name: live-run-monitoring-via-state-poll-plus-stream-tail
description: Monitoring a live K8s run: GET /runs/:id/events tails the live stream and never closes (a full download only completes at terminal), so poll run state via GET /runs/:id every ~55s and, to check progress, background-download the event stream to a file and inspect its tail — event ts freshness proves the agent is alive.

name: k8s-spot-preemption-classification
description: warren-ea4b: Spot preemption classified as a new retryable RunFailureReason 'preempted' (src/core/wire.ts + TerminalReason in runtime/contract.ts), witnesses in k8s/status-map.ts (reason Terminated/Shutdown + node-shutdown message, DisruptionTarget/TerminationByKubelet) and the vanished-pod arm via PodWatcher.deletedSpotNode + K8sProvider.preemptedPods; a 30s spot-node label poll in runtime-wiring.ts detects deleted gke-spot nodes. Ratchet note: provider.ts/wire.ts/contract.ts sit at frozen size ceilings — trimming pre-existing comment lines was required to add net code.

gVisor (GKE Sandbox) breaks warren's uid-1000 file-caps setpriv split: admission rejects allowPrivilegeEscalation=true, no_new_privs makes file caps inert, and gVisor drops ambient caps across a root->1000 setpriv (runc keeps them). setpriv also rejects --securebits +keep_caps. Working posture: entrypoint uid 0 inside the sandbox with caps SETUID/SETGID/KILL and allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, agent still dropped to 1001 (pod-runtime-class.ts).
resolution: Use resources.runtimeClass, which applies sandboxedAgentSecurityContext; never re-enable allowPrivilegeEscalation for sandboxed pods.

name: gvisor-spike-2026-09-25
description: Spike 2026-09-25 on GKE Autopilot: gVisor bun install --frozen-lockfile is 2.8x slower than runc (29.5s vs 10.7s); clone 1.2x, bun test 1.2x. Metadata server 169.254.169.254 was reachable from run pods on BOTH runtimes; only the NetworkPolicy except blocks it. us-west1 SSD_TOTAL_GB quota raised to 750 (each Autopilot node takes a 100GB boot disk).
